reasons: Same underlying quantity: postgresql.operations with operation=hot_upd counts hot-updated rows, which matches postgresql.rows_hot_updated, so a translated outcome is correct.
Datadog plots the raw metric with no rate() or rollup, but the candidate wraps it in rate(), changing the unit to rows per second versus the Datadog per-interval value.
Aggregation differs: Datadog uses avg by {db}, the candidate uses sum by (postgresql_database_name).

Template filters are dropped: $db (prefix db) should become a matcher on postgresql_database_name=~"$db" and $host (prefix host) should become host_name=~"$host" (host_name is observed in the dataset). The candidate applies neither, so the series set is wider than the Datadog request.
$table is not referenced in the Datadog query and is correctly absent; $scope has no prefix and default * so dropping it is correct.
Grouping by database name matches the Datadog by {db} grouping once the label is mapped to postgresql_database_name.
